posts.author: Sleeperr
posts.body:
I salute you.
Let me start with a premise, that "yes, I have seen many posts trying to resolve exact same issue", and yet I'd like a minute of your time. I genuinely ask for your patience and understanding, because I've spent weeks trying to solve this problem and feel like I'm going in circles. Thank you.
I am desperately trying to achieve a seemingly unachievable goal and that is to get the retro pixel perfect look for my game in RPGMakerMZ.
So far, I've tried every resolution and plugin I could find (and in some cases afford). But let's review some of the most prominent solutions I've already tried:
+
Visustella
- with nearest-neighbor rendering enabled to avoid blurriness - result: uneven, wonky pixels.
+
Hakuen Studio
- (integer scaling) + his
Pixel Perfect
plugin - the issue remains the same.
+
TDDP Pixel Perfect
- same effect.
+
San Hendrix
- Game Resolution - with integer scaling and pixel-perfect options enabled - same issue.
This led me to wonder if the problem was my monitor resolution rather than RPG Maker itself. So I tested multiple screen resolutions (my screen + different resolutions in the project system settings), but nothing helped.
So far the best results I was able to achieve is by setting the base resolution of the game to 640 x 360 and scale all the graphics and assets by 200% in Aseprite. By effectively doubling the pixel size, I eliminated most of the visual inconsistencies. The downside is that the game now appears less detailed because all of the graphics were originally designed with a
320×180
resolution in mind. Which is acceptable for a retro looking game. Also, this only looks decent in fullscreen or maximised window.
Win mode no scaling (2px wide blacklines):
Fullscreen automatic scaling (2px wide lines):
The results were stunning in my opinion, yet introducing 1px lines would cause problems.
However, the text remained a problem. Naturally I've tried to replace the font with bitmaps, after experimenting with several free solutions, I got
Hakuen Studio
Bitmap Font Pro. It worked alright until I ran into the issue shown below:
The pixels are clearly uneven because I wasn't able to apply "the double pixel rule" I invented as text would appear too large.
So my question to the community, is there a way to get the true pixel perfect look, or is it just a fantasy, a unattainable feature that was never intended by the developers of RPGMakerMZ?
If anyone has experience with this, or can explain what I'm missing, I would greatly appreciate the help xxx

posts.author: Kenen
posts.body:
This is not particularly difficult to do.
The correct way is to start with your base pixel grid and upscale your materials by 2-3x. 3x generally maps more directly to the 48px tilesets and is what you will often see done with 8- or 16-bit style resource packs.
The font is something I see overlooked a lot. You need to find a pixel font whose dimensions match your upscaling value. This means a font intended for 8px use being used at 24px, or 10px to 30px (if you are using a 3x scale).
Your selected font should have the same pixel ratio as your tiles and other assets. If your letters are 1px wide at their thinnest point while your tilesets are at 200% size, the font is wrong.
You also can’t put a 1px outline around your font if your base pixel scale is 2px.
Depending on how great your attention to detail is, you should also be clamping the x and y coordinates of any UI elements to multiples of your scale factor (e.g. 2 or 3). Window and gauge sizes should be clamped similarly.

posts.author: KaijuuKimi
posts.body:
The previous plugin might be to hard to use because it is in jp
I'll provide this instead
1. insert
DP MapZoom
and TDDP pixel perfect
2. open system 2 and set your screen and ui to 960x540 (x3 of your 320x180)
3 set DP Magnification to 3 (or 2 if you like. Other option you can decide yorself)
4.set TDDP enable ingame option to true. open game and set the perfect pixel to on and stretching to off and quit to title screen (it is bugged by default in mz so need to do this)
5. the map will be x3 without resizing and game should look pixel perfect
